audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 1 and 2 were scored 'Skill' while whys[0], spikes[0] and the whole early paragraph say Trundle wins them outright ('this is your clearest window in the whole matchup'). Level 6 was scored 'Skill' while whys[4] hands it to Ryze.
audit.why: Trundle is at 51.83% over 164 games — a lane he shades. The old chart gave him nothing at any stage while the prose gave him the first two levels, so neither the numbers nor the text matched the card.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Trundle / Trundle / Skill / Ryze / Ryze / Skill / Ryze in both layers. Two Trundle stages, three Ryze, two even — which is what a 51.83% lane that front-loads and then scales away actually looks like.

audit.whatIsWrong: Realm Warp was described twice as an escape — 'his Realm Warp escape option' and 'Subjugate cannot generate value if he warps out of the all-in before the second cast lands'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Ryze creates a portal, and after a few seconds allies standing near it are teleported. It is a delayed group reposition on a 180/160/140s cooldown, not a blink out of your ultimate. A Trundle who believes it is an escape will decline all-ins he wins.
audit.corrected: Level 6 rewritten around what Realm Warp actually is — a 180s map-tempo tool at rank 1 — while keeping the stage as Ryze's, because the map pressure is real even though the escape is not.

audit.whatIsWrong: The root is attributed to the wrong abilities everywhere: 'Q+E root combo', 'his E root', 'Root you with W or the E+Q combo'. Rune Prison (W, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, 615 range) slows on its own and only ROOTS a target already carrying the Spell Flux (E) debuff. Overload never roots. Chomp's sap is also called an 'AS debuff' in whys[3]; it saps attack damage.
audit.why: This is the whole defensive read of the lane. The root has a prerequisite, and the prerequisite is a separate 615-range cast — so Spell Flux is the thing you watch, and if it misses, Rune Prison is only a slow you can walk out of inside Frozen Domain.
audit.corrected: Spell Flux named as the prerequisite in spikes[1], whys[1], whys[2], mid and breakdown.cooldowns, with Rune Prison's 11s rank-1 cooldown and the slow-versus-root distinction stated.

audit.why: Rune Prison is 11s at rank 1 while Spell Flux is 3.5s and Overload is reset by every other basic — so the long cooldown in his kit is exactly the one that locks you down. Ryze also pays 40 to 90 mana per cast, and his passive scales off bonus mana, so early spam has a real cost.
audit.corrected: 'Bite in the beat after Spell Flux misses; Rune Prison is 11s at rank 1' written into whys[1], mid and breakdown.cooldowns, plus the mana-cost punish in early.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Shadowflame burst ignores the resistances Subjugate steals' and 'Full AP Ryze with Shadowflame ignores your MR steal entirely'.
audit.why: Magic penetration reduces magic resist; it does not make it irrelevant, and Subjugate takes a percent of his resists AND his health while adding both to you. Telling a player his ultimate is worthless in the matchup removes his best button.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as penetration cutting into the steal rather than cancelling it, with the advice kept (ult the frontliner in a 5v5) but justified honestly.

edits.before: Ryze's Q+E root combo comes fully online — he can lock you in place and stack flux for burst; respect the root range and don't chase him straight.
edits.after: Spell Flux into Rune Prison (11s at rank 1) is the root — the cage only holds a Flux'd target, so the orb is the cast you have to dodge.

edits.before: Ryze's Realm Warp enables team roams and his damage output jumps; his ranged burst through your MR starts outpacing what Subjugate can repay at this stage.
edits.after: Realm Warp (180s at rank 1) is a delayed portal for his whole team, not a blink — his damage jumps at 6, but the map pressure is what actually costs you here.

edits.before: Seraph's + Shadowflame Ryze deletes you through your resistances — even Subjugate's MR drain doesn't offset the AP scaling damage he outputs at 2+ items.
edits.after: Seraph's plus Shadowflame lets Ryze burn through most of what Subjugate steals back — penetration cuts into the drain, so pick the frontliner and not him.

edits.before: Force W-inside all-ins at level 1 and 2 before Ryze's Q+E root combo is ranked up enough to punish your approach
edits.after: All-in inside Frozen Domain at levels 1 and 2, before Spell Flux into Rune Prison is ranked enough to hold you

edits.before: Root you with W or the E+Q combo to break your Frozen Domain pattern and prevent extended trades
edits.after: Land Spell Flux first so Rune Prison roots instead of slowing, then break your Frozen Domain pattern

edits.before: Spam Q resets to whittle your HP from range while you can't close the gap cleanly
edits.after: Reset Overload off every other cast and chip you from 1000 range while you close

edits.before: Use Realm Warp to leave the losing lane entirely and generate advantages elsewhere on the map
edits.after: Use Realm Warp to move the fight somewhere Trundle is not, instead of trying to duel him

edits.before: His Q+E root is only one rank deep — short trades inside Frozen Domain are roughly even, but he can kite you off the zone if he respects the matchup.
edits.after: Rune Prison is 11s at rank 1 and only roots a Flux'd target — short trades inside Frozen Domain are even, but he kites you off the zone if you walk straight.

edits.before: Ryze's E root becomes a reliable all-in setup at level 3; his Q resets through flux stacks start outpacing the healing your W provides if he can root you first.
edits.after: At 3 the Spell Flux into Rune Prison root is reliable, and his Overload resets start outpacing your W healing once the cage lands — but the orb has to land first.

edits.before: Ranked-up flux combos deal more burst per rotation than your Frozen Domain can offset, and he simply backs off when Chomp's AS debuff slows his Q reset rhythm.
edits.after: Ranked flux combos out-burst what Frozen Domain can offset per rotation, and he backs off the moment Chomp's AD sap and slow break his Overload reset rhythm.

edits.before: Realm Warp makes him effectively uncatchable when he does not want to fight; Subjugate cannot generate value if he warps out of the all-in before the second cast lands.
edits.after: Realm Warp is a 180-second portal that moves his team, not a blink out of your all-in — level 6 goes to him on map tempo, not because Subjugate stops working.

edits.before: Full AP Ryze with Shadowflame ignores your MR steal entirely; Subjugate is better spent on an enemy tank in 5v5 — do not try to duel Ryze in a side lane at this stage.
edits.after: Shadowflame penetration eats into the MR you steal, so Subjugate pays more on an enemy tank in a 5v5 — pick your side-lane fights with Pillar of Ice, he has no dash.

edits.before: Chomp wins you level 1 — step into Ryze's auto range before he levels E and bite him the instant he last-hits. The AD steal and King's Tribute healing from minion deaths mean even a glancing trade is net positive for you. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain directly under your feet and force the zone trade: your movement speed advantage closes the gap his short legs need to kite. This is your clearest window in the whole matchup — Ryze's Q+E root is not yet threatening enough to punish a disciplined W-inside approach, and he cannot out-sustain the combined healing from your domain and passive.
edits.after: Chomp wins you level 1 — step into Ryze's auto range before he ranks Spell Flux and bite him the instant he last-hits. The AD sap plus King's Tribute healing off dying minions makes even a glancing trade net positive. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain directly under your feet and force the zone trade: the move speed closes the gap he needs to kite. This is your clearest window in the whole matchup. Watch his mana too — Spell Flux and Rune Prison cost up to 75 and 90, and his passive scales off bonus mana, so every spammed poke wave is damage he cannot spend on you later.

edits.before: Once Ryze hits level 3 and ranks E, his Q+E root string locks you in place long enough for him to stack flux and repeat fire — never walk straight at him or he will chain two rooted bursts together. Use Pillar of Ice not as a chase tool but as a pathing block: throw it to his side to cut off the lateral movement he needs to avoid Frozen Domain. Level 6 feels like it should be your spike, but Ryze's ranged burst through your resistances and his Realm Warp escape option mean you rarely get a clean Subjugate all-in; use it if he overextends, but don't force it into his full kit.
edits.after: From level 3 the root is real, but read it correctly: Rune Prison (11s at rank 1) only roots a target already debuffed by Spell Flux, so the orb is the cast you dodge and the cage is what you punish. If Spell Flux misses, the cage is a slow you can walk out of inside Frozen Domain, and Chomp is back every 3.5 seconds. Use Pillar of Ice as a pathing block rather than a chase tool — Ryze has no dash, so terrain to his side takes away the lateral step he needs to leave your zone. Level 6 goes to him on map tempo: Realm Warp is a 180-second portal for his whole team, not an escape, so keep taking the all-in when Rune Prison is down.

edits.before: Ryze owns the late game decisively. His Seraph's Embrace into Shadowflame burst ignores the resistances Subjugate steals, and his Realm Warp turns him into a global threat your side-lane pressure cannot match. Your job is to use Subjugate on the tankiest frontliner in 5v5 fights — not Ryze himself — and let the resist-drain carry team fights rather than trying to duel him one-on-one. The lane was always borrowed time; convert early gold into objectives before his second item comes in.
edits.after: Ryze owns the late game on scaling. Seraph's Embrace into Shadowflame penetrates much of what Subjugate steals back, and Realm Warp turns him into a map threat your side-lane pressure cannot match. Your job in a 5v5 is to Subjugate the tankiest frontliner rather than Ryze himself and let the drain carry the fight. If he does step into a side lane, take it — he has no dash and Pillar of Ice is a 21-second wall he has to walk around. The lane was always borrowed time; convert early gold into objectives before his second item lands.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison: matchup-defining — His point-blank root — sets up his combo. Bait it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Rune Prison (W): 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s. Roots only a Spell Flux'd target — dodge the orb, then punish the cage.

edits.before: Track Ryze's Rune Prison: His point-blank root — sets up his combo. Bait it. When it is down — Bite + W-zone duel.
edits.after: Rune Prison roots only a Spell Flux'd target, and it is 11s at rank 1. Dodge the orb — then bite and W-zone duel.

edits.before: Pillar closes the kit — use it behind Ryze to deny disengage, or between you and Rune Prison to break his pattern.
edits.after: Pillar of Ice closes your kit and Ryze has no dash to cross it — put it to his side to take the step he kites with.

edits.before: Q ranks raise the bite damage and the AD steal. Keep trading in W; if Ryze stands in your domain trading evenly, he is losing.
edits.after: His ranked flux rotations out-burst your zone healing. Trade only after Spell Flux misses, and let Chomp's sap break his rhythm.

edits.before: Subjugate online — the 1v1 is yours into almost anyone the moment Ryze commits. R early in the all-in so the drained resists count for the whole fight.
edits.after: Realm Warp is a 180s portal for his team rather than an escape, so it costs you map tempo, not duels. Subjugate still wins the 1v1 when Rune Prison is down.
